title: Jucy, Mustardy Greek Spinach and Feta Spanakopita
description: A comforting, fluffy, and flavorful Greek dish with a tangy twist, perfect for a weeknight dinner.

ingredients.name: appleton rum
ingredients.notes: do not omit, but be careful not to burn the phyllo

ingredients.name: yuzu-cured sea salt
ingredients.notes: optional, but recommended for added depth

instructions: Thaw the phyllo dough according to the package instructions.
In a medium skillet, sauté the chopped onion in 1 tablespoon of the melted butter until translucent.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked onion, spinach, feta cheese, mustard, rum, and yuzu-cured sea salt (if using).
In a separate mixing bowl, mix the remaining 1 tablespoon of melted butter with a little water to create a brushable consistency.
Layer the phyllo dough in a 9x13 inch baking dish, brushing each layer with the butter mixture and folding the dough in a zig-zag pattern to create a lattice top.
Pour the spinach mixture into the center of the baking dish, leaving a 1-inch border around the edges.
Fold the edges of the phyllo dough over the filling, pressing gently to seal.
Brush the top of the phyllo dough with the remaining butter mixture.
Bake the spanakopita in the preheated oven for 35-40 minutes, or until the phyllo is golden brown and puffed.
Remove from the oven and let cool for 10 minutes before slicing and serving.
Serve warm, garnished with additional feta cheese and a sprinkle of yuzu-cured sea salt (if desired).
